body:
Found by the first cold start on a repo that is not hkb on 2026-08-27 (a private, org-owned monorepo with live CI).

`installStopHook` (`src/init.js:99-119`) writes **two** hooks into `.claude/settings.json` — `ensure('Stop', ...)` and `ensure('PreToolUse', ...)` at lines 116-117 — but init logs only:

    added Stop hook to .claude/settings.json (inert unless KB_TASK is set)

The adopter found the `PreToolUse` entry by reading `git diff`, not from our output. `hkb help` under `plumbing` also lists only `hook stop`, while `src/cli.js:210` already knows `hkb hook stop|pretool`.

**The hook is correct and must stay on by default.** It is hkb's permission policy for workers — "allow or deny, never a prompt" (`src/hook.js:31`): file tools are confined to the worktree, five patterns are hard-denied (`hkb dispatch`, `pkill`/`kill`, force-push, `sudo`, `rm -rf <abs>` — `src/model.js:433-439`), and everything else is checked against the profile allowlist. Without it, a dispatched worker stalls on the first permission prompt with nobody there to answer. It is inert outside a worker: `src/hook.js:33` returns before it reads stdin unless `KB_TASK` is set.

So this is a disclosure bug, not a design one. Writing a repo-wide `matcher: "*"` hook into a settings file the operator shares with every other session in that repo, and not saying so, is value 4 ("never a silent failure") inverted.

**Fix.**
- Init names both hooks and says what the second one is for, e.g. `added Stop and PreToolUse hooks to .claude/settings.json (both inert unless KB_TASK is set; PreToolUse is the worker permission policy)`.
- The `plumbing` line in `HELP` becomes `hook stop|pretool`.
- Rename `installStopHook` to match what it installs.

**Verify.** A fresh `init` prints both; a re-run reports both already present; the settings.json shape assertions in `test/harness.test.js` cover it.
title: init installs two hooks and reports one
